catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds an oscilloscope's identity, timebase and vertical settings: cap.measure.voltage.v1 is one DC or RMS voltage on instrument.dmm, instrument.smu or sensor; cap.sensing.read.v1 binds sensor, sensor.imu and sensor.force_torque and reports sensor channel values, not the displayed channels' settings; cap.device.configure.v1 is the write class; cap.device.describe.v1 is deprecated and describes the MHS manifest, not the instrument. The extension returns the identity, the active channels and the timebase and vertical scale and offset read with the clone's :TIM:SCAL?, :TIM:OFFS?, :<CHANn>:SCAL? and :<CHANn>:OFFS? queries.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/pmezydlo__oscilloscope_lan_data_capture --backend fake (exit 0). All gates G1 to G7 and G9 passed; G8 warns only G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE because the package declares no Limit, so the suite has no out-of-limit input to probe and awards CL2 while every other CL3 test passed. That is expected for this package: the clone sends no numeric instrument setting, so no bound is invented from the constructor's channel count, a sample capture or a default, and there is no site-limits overlay. The evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card proposes a SerialDriver (family serial, decision family-config), but the clone assembles every channel command at run time (":" + check_chan + ":DISP?" and ":" + channel + ":SCAL?") and a fixed command table cannot reproduce the lines the device receives (G7). This package is a direct Driver over oscilloscope_functions:oscilloscope and calls the clone's own methods and queries. No hardware backend is registered: the clone is Python 2 code (its LAN transport is a copy of the Python 2.7 telnetlib, telnetlib_receive_all.py:1-2, imported by the device constructor, and its serial path passes text to serial.write), while this package runs on Python 3. The fake backend is the only backend and the acceptance gate is the only evidence; no hardware was attached and no hardware run is claimed.

Covered: the four identity fields the clone parses from *IDN? (manufacturer, device name, serial number, firmware version); the active-channel list captured by get_active_channel() at connect; the timebase scale and offset (:TIM:SCAL?, :TIM:OFFS?); and x-cap.pmezydlo.settings.v1, a read extension returning the identity, the active channels, the timebase and the vertical scale and offset of each active channel (:<CHANn>:SCAL?, :<CHANn>:OFFS?). No write, no numeric input and no Limit: the clone sets no numeric setting, so the package has no bounds and no operator-required paths.

NOT COVERED: the waveform array and the PNG plot. plot() reads :WAV:DATA? as text, drops 10 header characters and builds voltage and time arrays, but it references tUnit at line 62 while only commented-out code names it (lines 50-57), so the method cannot complete; the package reads the scalar settings with the same queries and does not transfer samples. The :WAV:POIN:MODE RAW and :KEY:FORCE writes are not exposed. The LAN, USB and RS232 transports are not exercised because no hardware backend exists.

The upstream clone stayed read-only at commit f68c0b8d5acb7592ad21fd39b453d5a4d892a91e (G1). The clone has no simulator and no recording, and a strict transcript would replay one fixed request sequence while the gate and the conformance suite send many; the fake is an in-memory stand-in whose replies use the exact queries of the clone. Its values are placeholder test data, never Facts, Limits or references. This package is model-authored by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 (run wP-025) and unreviewed; driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null, no human reviewed or tested it, and no hardware run is claimed. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; gate.digest is the digest the last check printed.
